compute.title: Compute Detector
compute.what_can_train: What can realistically be trained on this server

recommendation.gpu: A GPU was detected ({{names}}). Depending on VRAM, you can consider LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning for models up to 7–13B, or full training of smaller models. The list of models that fit your free VRAM is on /compute/allowed-models.
recommendation.minimal: No GPU detected, and available RAM is under 4 GB. Only the simplest classic models (logistic regression, shallow decision trees) on small tabular datasets are realistic. Fine-tuning any NLP/LLM model on this server is not recommended.
recommendation.cpu_classic: No GPU detected, and RAM is limited. Classic ML (scikit-learn, XGBoost) on tabular data works well. Inference for small NLP models (DistilBERT-class) is possible, but training them on CPU will be slow and only feasible on very small datasets.
recommendation.cpu_light_nlp: No GPU detected, but RAM is enough for classic ML at full scale. Light fine-tuning of very small NLP models on CPU is technically possible but will take hours even on modest datasets — use it only for experiments, not regular training.
recommendation.cpu_generous: No GPU detected, but RAM is generous. Classic ML with no practical memory limits. CPU training of small transformer models is possible, but remains orders of magnitude slower than GPU — for serious LLM fine-tuning, a cloud GPU is still recommended.

warnings_map.low_vram: Low free VRAM ({{vram_free_gb}} GB) — even small models may not fit, especially if the GPU is already busy.
